annotation.cut_point:
We are given a problem involving 10 people and a test with several questions. The conditions are:

- **Any group of 5 people together answered all the questions** (i.e., for each question, at least one of the 5 people in the group answered it correctly).
- **Any group of 4 people did not** (i.e., for each question, **none** of the 4 people in the group answered it correctly).

verified_state: There are 10 people and several questions.
Any group of 5 people together answered all the questions: for each question and each 5-person group, at least one person in that group gave the correct answer.
reflection.error_step: - **Any group of 4 people did not** (i.e., for each question, **none** of the 4 people in the group answered it correctly).
reflection.error_reason: This misinterprets the second condition. It should mean that for every group of four people, there exists at least one question that none of them answered correctly, not that this holds separately for every question.
reflection.new_direction: Correct the quantifier and define, for each question, the set of people who answered incorrectly; then require every 4-person subset to be contained in at least one such incorrect set.
